issues.description: The problem statement requires Farm to store animals in a List and explicitly asks to implement it using an ArrayList initialized in the no-argument constructor. The solution implementation instead declares the animals attribute as a Queue and initializes it with a LinkedList. This diverges from the specified type (List/ArrayList) and from the constructor requirement, which can confuse students about the intended collection type and may cause tests or grading checks that expect a List/ArrayList to fail.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the solution's Farm use the collection type specified in the problem: declare the animals attribute as a List<Animal> and initialize it with a new ArrayList<>() in the no-argument constructor. Update the getter and setter to use List<Animal> as well. Alternatively, if Queue/LinkedList is intentional, update the problem statement and UML to accept Queue/LinkedList instead.
